description: SYNC SNDFILE MIDTIMES: builds (or rebuilds) a mixfile in which every sound's MIDPOINT lands at the same instant - CDP reads each file's real duration from disk and computes the start times (verified: 1 s / 2 s / 1.5 s files -> starts 0.5 / 0.0 / 0.25, all midpoints at 1.0; earliest start is always 0). The intextfile aux is EITHER a bare list of sndfile names (one per line; output lines get level 1.0 and pan 'C') OR an existing mixfile (levels and pans are PRESERVED and the lines are re-sorted into the new time order - verified). Sub-directory paths pass through intact ('sub/n1.wav' verified) and the output renders directly through submix mix (round-trip verified, 2.0 s from a 2 s longest file). This is audio-aware text generation - the durations come from the soundfile headers, which is why it earns an entry over hand-editing. Deterministic (byte-identical). Sibling submode 2 aligns ENDTIMES instead.
musical_use: Centre-alignment for layered stacks: swells, cymbal rolls, reversed-attack pads and other symmetric gestures read as 'together' when their CENTRES coincide, not their starts - sync 1 computes that alignment for any mix of lengths in one call. Classic uses: stack N variants of a gesture (different processings, different rates) so their energy peaks pile up at one moment; centre a short accent inside a long bed; rebuild an existing mixfile (levels/pans kept) after swapping sounds of different lengths via submix model-style edits. The output is a normal mixfile - re-level it with submix attenuate, re-position with submix pan, check headroom with getlevel 3 (midpoint pile-ups sum hot by design!), then render with submix mix.

intextfile.description: EITHER a plain list of soundfile names (one per line, cwd-relative; write with write_data_file()) OR an existing mixfile whose levels/pans should survive re-timing. Renders in the argv BEFORE the output path. A missing/invalid name refuses 'Application doesn't work with this type of infile.' (exit 255). NOTE: sample rates are NOT validated here - a mixed-rate list is accepted (verified exit 0) and the refusal only surfaces downstream at submix mix time.

examples.description: Centre-align three swell variants into one mixfile.
examples.expected_use: write_data_file('swells.txt', 'inputs/sw1.wav\ninputs/sw2.wav\ngraphs/<gid>/sw3.wav'). Output lines carry level 1.0 - run getlevel 3 before rendering (midpoints sum hot).

examples.description: Re-time an existing mix so all centres coincide, keeping its levels and pans.
examples.expected_use: Levels/pans preserved, lines re-sorted into the new time order; render via submix mix.

known_issues: Bare-list outputs use pan letter 'C' - which submix mix treats as NO-PAN, not centre (tranche-5 finding): an all-mono synced list renders MONO. That is usually what you want; for true centre-panned stereo replace C with numeric 0 (or run spacewarp/pan). Also feed such files through submix attenuate/pan only AFTER giving lines numeric pans (pan's no-pan path is broken - see that entry).
NO SAMPLE-RATE VALIDATION: a list mixing 44.1 kHz and 22.05 kHz files is accepted (exit 0, verified) and the mismatch only refuses later at submix mix. Check rates when assembling the list.

Midpoint alignment stacks every file's loudest region at one instant by design - ALWAYS pre-flight with submix getlevel 3 before rendering at the default level-1.0 lines (overload at the mix stage WRAPS).
Mixed mono/stereo lists are fine (verified: stereo entries come out in the 'name time 2 level L level R' form; mix accepts it).

The output is a DATA file (mixfile, .txt): consumer = submix mix's mixfile parameter or the other mixfile entries. Duration pre-flight skipped ('static' is a placeholder); the rendered duration = the longest file when midpoints coincide.
Deterministic: byte-identical output run to run. No numeric parameters at all.
Arity-0 entry (sources named inside the aux list): call process() with no input argument. duration_row null in the findings (data output).
